actions.description: Publish one joint-angle command to a leg's position controller. The angle is the value before the per-leg JOINT_OFFSET; the upstream method adds that fixed offset and publishes a std_msgs/Float64. The receipt confirms that the message was handed to the publisher, not that the joint moved or reached the target.

inputs.name: leg

inputs.description: Joint within the leg, mapped through LegController.joint_name
inputs.name: joint

inputs.description: Joint angle before the fixed per-leg JOINT_OFFSET
inputs.name: angle_rad

actions.description: Command the four legs to the upstream fixed stand end-effector pose. This is an active posture command, not a stop or a measured stand: the position controllers provide no quiescence acknowledgement, so it is not a safe-state action and is refused while the e-stop is latched.
actions.name: stand

outputs.description: Legs commanded to the stand pose
outputs.name: legs

outputs.description: True when the stand publication calls were made
outputs.name: commanded

outputs.description: Always false: the upstream publisher has no posture or quiescence acknowledgement
outputs.name: confirmed

facts.text: The README describes the repository as a quadrupedal robot simulation by ROS and Gazebo.
The README quick start launches cheetah_gazebo, cheetah_control and the cheetah_core stand_demo script.
LegController stores the leg name, the joint_name list of hip/thigh/calf, the leg's fixed JOINT_OFFSET and three publisher objects.

LegController builds each command topic by concatenating /cheetah/, the leg name, _joint, the 1-based joint index and _position_controller/command, and creates a rospy Publisher of Float64 with queue_size 5 on it.
_writeJointPosInRad adds the leg's fixed joint offset to the requested angle and publishes the sum as a Float64 message.
writeEndPos runs inverseKinematics on the end-effector position and writes the three resulting joint angles.
The __main__ block of legController.py ends with the Python 2 print statement print "hello world".
Cheetah.__init__ stores the leg_names list and a controllers dict that maps each leg name to a LegController.
Cheetah.stand commands each of the four legs to a fixed end-effector pose through writeEndPos.
Cheetah.run calls stand every 0.1 s until rospy shuts down, and the script's main initialises the anonymous node control_node and runs it.
trot_demo.py's trot writes each leg's computed end position through self.controllers[leg].writeEndPos, and its run calls trot with the elapsed ROS time every 0.01 s until rospy shuts down.
The control launch spawns twelve position controllers and the joint_state_controller under the /cheetah namespace.
The controller configuration loads joint_state_controller with publish_rate 50 and twelve effort_controllers/JointPositionController entries.
The URDF's gazebo_ros_control plugin declares robotNamespace /cheetah and robotSimType gazebo_ros_control/DefaultRobotHWSim.
The URDF declares the leg joint LF_JOINT1 as a continuous joint without a limit element.
settings.py defines BODY_LENGTH, BODY_WIDTH, the hip, thigh and calf lengths in LEG_LENGTH, LEG_NAME and the per-leg JOINT_OFFSET values.
The Gazebo launch includes empty_world.launch with paused=true and spawns the cheetah model from the URDF.

determinism.notes: Event-driven Python fake with no physics step, ROS graph, controller dynamics or wall-clock pacing; placeholder joint and stand state does not establish a trajectory or state-hash replay

gaps: the fake is an analytic Python stand-in for the upstream Python 2/rospy publisher, not a recording of captured ROS traffic and not the Gazebo simulator; it runs no physics, contacts, controller dynamics or IK

the twelve /cheetah/<leg>_joint<N>_position_controller/command topics are assembled at legController.py:23; the fake publishes no ROS messages and no live ROS backend is declared or run by this simulated package

the upstream stand command is an active posture command, not a stop: the e-stop sends it and then reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held, and no joint-state, TF, IMU or contact observation confirms that the robot stopped

the README's stand_demo node republishes the stand pose every 0.1 s and trot_demo publishes a trot gait every 0.01 s on the same twelve topics (stand_demo.py:28-31, trot_demo.py:93-97); while either runs it overrides this package's joint and stand commands

the native modules are Python 2 code (print statements at legController.py:48 and InverseKinematics.py:57; InverseKinematics.py:4 imports settings as an implicit relative import): the native class cannot be imported by the SDK's Python 3, so no live backend can construct it
the gate's call recorder does not trace calls on objects inside the upstream controllers dict, so it cannot see the per-joint publication of the leg command (only the fake's own record does)
the /cheetah/joint_states topic from the joint_state_controller and the IMU plugin are not exposed; there is no read-back of the commanded joint positions
the Gazebo launch starts the world paused=true (cheetah.launch:4); the operator must unpause it and the fake does not model pause/unpause
the upstream controllers, Gazebo physics and rosbridge are ROS 1 components; no ROS graph, Gazebo process, rosbridge connection or hardware was started or tested here
the fake's joint and stand values are placeholders; the real stand pose and IK are in stand_demo.py:20-26 and InverseKinematics.py:6-51 and are not used as facts

operator_required.name: move_joint
operator_required.reason: the pinned URDF declares the leg joints continuous and the controller config states no joint-position limit; the deployment operator supplies the joint-angle envelope in site-limits.json

safe_state.description: No safe state is certified: the e-stop sends the Cheetah.stand posture (twelve unacknowledged Float64 setpoints) and reports SAFE_STATE_UNREACHED with the latch held; Gazebo keeps simulating, nothing senses quiescence, a running stand_demo (0.1 s) or trot_demo (0.01 s) node overrides the setpoints, and the legs track whatever setpoint the position controllers received last.
